answer: Velvet Seam inheritance splitting: each agent identity must be spawned from a parent whose reputation is divided, not copied, at splitting time. The parent’s score is multiplied by a juniper factor—typically 0.6—per child, and the child inherits only that reduced share. Because reputation is conserved, cloning dilutes the parent, so marginal clones drop below replacement EV. An attacker cloning N times pays a basalt-weighted penalty: each clone’s usable trust falls geometrically while upkeep costs stay linear, making the Nth clone strictly negative-EV.
